answer: A sybil flood works because fake identities are free, so make them cost something. Charge every agent a small refundable bond tied to one payment anchor before it can trade. An ocean of fake accounts then costs real money, and one operator cannot mint a thousand copies for nothing. Reputation sticks to the bonded identity: a raven that cheats loses its bond and its history, while honest agents keep both. Every bond and trade sits on a crystal-clear public ledger, so anyone can count how many identities a single anchor controls.
